prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” broker for every self‑employed person — the right broker depends on your budget, whether you want in‑person help, whether you need an ACA/Marketplace plan (with premium tax credits) or a private/short‑term plan, your preferred doctors/networks, and whether you have any employees. I can help you find one, but first a few quick questions:

- Do you want an in‑person/local agent in Kansas City, or are you OK with a reputable online broker?
- Are you shopping for an individual/Family ACA plan (Healthcare.gov), a small‑group plan for a business with employees, or something else (COBRA, short‑term, Medicare, etc.)?
- What’s your ZIP code (so I can narrow to agents licensed in your area)?
- Any must‑have features (HSA eligibility, specific providers, low deductible, dental/vision, budget target)?

How to choose a great broker for someone self‑employed
- Use an independent broker who can compare multiple carriers (not a captive agent who only sells one insurer).  
- Confirm they’re licensed in Missouri (ask to see their license number).  
- Look for specific experience with self‑employed clients and ACA subsidies (estimating net premium after tax credits).  
- Ask whether they charge a client fee or are paid only by carriers (transparency on fees).  
- Prefer brokers who provide year‑round support (help with mid‑year life changes, claims issues, renewals).  
- Check reviews on Google/Yelp, NAHU (National Association of Health Underwriters) listings, and the Missouri Dept. of Insurance consumer resources.

Questions to ask prospective brokers
- How many individual/sole‑proprietor clients do you serve?  
- Which carriers do you represent, and can you show multiple plan comparisons?  
- Do you help with Marketplace enrollment and subsidy calculations?  
- Do you charge any fees? If so, how much and for what services?  
- Will you help with claims/appeals and year‑round issues?  
- Can you estimate my net monthly cost after subsidies? What documents do you need from me?

Places to search for vetted brokers
- HealthCare.gov broker/assister locator (for ACA certified navigators/agents).  
- NAHU “Find an Agent” tool.  
- Missouri Department of Insurance consumer help for licensed agents.  
- Local Google/Yelp searches for “independent health insurance agent Kansas City MO.”

Alternatives and things to consider
- Online brokers like eHealth or GoHealth can be fast and compare carriers, but may not provide local, ongoing support.  
- Short‑term plans exist but have major coverage limits — not usually a safe substitute for ACA coverage.  
- If you hire staff or want to reimburse premiums, ask about QSEHRA/ICHRA options — a good broker can advise on tax and compliance issues.

If you want, give me your ZIP code and whether you prefer in‑person or online help and I’ll put together a short list of well‑matched brokers/agents in the Kansas City area and sample questions/emails you can send them.
